decisions: forge.action.combat.projectile_fire is implemented against the ruled shape (design fwd-combat section 4): the projectile:resource/model input is replaced by the structural parameter projectile_type (the native ProjectileType enum), and the destination is ProjectileManager.WantToFireTargeting.

The runtime speed input the ruled shape keeps has no native destination in pFireTargeting (six fields, none of them a speed), so a non-zero speed is refused by name instead of being ignored; the native per-shot speed lives on the prefab.

forge.action.combat.projectile_redirect writes ProjectileBase.m_myFwd (heading) and ProjectileBase.m_targetAgent (guide target) on the ProjectileTargeting instance this slice registered. Projectile.SetVelocity is deliberately not used: Projectile and ProjectileTargeting are two independent carriers and the manager's targeting path spawns the latter.

forge.action.combat.projectile_destroy calls ProjectileBase.DelayedDestroySelf with the component's own game object. impact_policy=detonate is refused because the explosion belongs to the projectile's own impact path (m_impactEffect, m_projectileExplosionForce, m_explosionTargetMask), which this call does not take.

forge.action.combat.projectile_bounce writes ProjectileBase.m_ricochetAngleThreshold. The native bounce has no count, restitution, speed loss or damage scale, so none of the removed inputs is accepted.

gtfo.projectile is registered by this slice because the four rows cannot be reached without it: the plan loader validates every entity input against a registered namespace resolver, and every projectile reference this slice hands out is its own SpawnProjectileType result. The entity instance resolver maps the native ProjectileTargeting back to that reference, so the kernel's own ResolveEntityInstance answers for this kind.
uncertainties: The sibling slice `C-projectile-facts` was authored in the same worktree and also registers the `gtfo.projectile` entity kind (ForgeEnemy/Native/ProjectileModule.cs, ProjectileFacts.Wire), naming a life from ProjectileBase.Pointer. This slice registers the same kind from its own table and names a life from its own counter. The kernel's resolver and instance-resolver tables are keyed by kind, so one registration replaces the other silently and one slice's references stop resolving. Exactly one owner must be chosen before the integration batch wires either slice; see %TEMP%/fan/c-projectile-actions/integration.json, notes[0].

ProjectileManager.SpawnProjectileType is invoked directly rather than through the broadcast action. The broadcast path (WantToFireTargeting -> m_fireTargeting -> DoFireTargeting) is the replication the design names, but it returns void, so nothing could be registered for redirect/destroy/bounce and the host could not answer for what it fired. The fire therefore goes through the same spawn entry the broadcast receiver uses, on the host only, and the native method bodies that would prove the two paths converge are not present in the interop assembly.

Whether a non-host that received the broadcast also spawns its own copy is not observable from the interop assembly; if it does, a host-side redirect is a host-side write to a replica's own component. This is on the in-game confirmation list together with evidence.md section 6 item 3.

ProjectileBase.m_ricochetAngleThreshold's native unit. The interop exposes a field accessor only, so this slice writes the number unchanged and declares the port's unit as deg in the contract; an in-game probe should confirm whether the native value is radians.

ProjectileTargeting.Speed is writable and is what the native movement reads each frame; mapping the ruled shape's speed input onto it would change one shot's flight speed, but only if the native movement multiplies by it every frame rather than caching a derived value. Not implemented without that evidence.
